formats.apdu: lowercase hex, CLA INS P1 P2 Lc data; Lc is the data's length, at most 255 (ledger.json's APDUs are hw-transport's framing of hw-app-eth's sends).
formats.rows: design 0016's rows in order: each APDU's header, its data, how many, where its bytes come from, and whether it waits for the user.
formats.checked: every APDU ledger.json records was checked against its row: the stream the design predicts for the case (honest, with the case's deviations applied as the design describes the reference: no B0 01 for a transaction or a message, app-check; E0 02 00 00 for ledger.add, address-from-device; hw-app-eth's cut, count and UTF-16 name lengths, field-pieces, device-bounds and name-ascii; the hash-only APDU after any 6D00 of signEIP712Message, blind-typed-data; nothing past the address check for a type 2 at a chain ID of 2^53 or more, chain-id-width; hw-app-eth's splitPath, path-strict; every listed record's path read after discovery, where the core reads a scheme's path only, path-strict, and at most 20, check-bound), up to where the case stopped (a fault in discovery's check ends the check, not discovery), and every deviation that makes it differ is marked on the case. `reached`: the honest APDUs of each row.
formats.honest: each complete operation's stream as the core sends it (ledger.json's case `case`), which main's relay admits; for a hash-only case, through the 6D00 and the hash-only APDU; for discovery, its paths and then its check of the case's `records` (each one's path, a scheme's only, at most 20: D1).
formats.refused: the cases the core refuses before the first APDU, by deviation.
formats.forbidden: single APDUs main refuses with `rule`, each at position `at` of the case's honest stream (the APDUs before it as honest): `what` says what changed; `parent` the parent it names; `state` what main holds then.
formats.same_shape: for each typed-data case the core sends, another schema and message of the same shape (every type and field name moved one letter on, EIP712Domain kept, every value another of the same encoded length) and its whole stream: the same headers and counts, other bytes, refused payload.
formats.name_ascii: for each name-ascii case, the reference's definition APDUs (a name's length byte in UTF-16 units), which the core never sends: refused payload.
formats.safe_changes: the SafeTx and SafeMessage of 0002's cases with one thing changed (each of the ten fields, the Safe's address, the chain, the digest): the typed data and the first APDU where its stream leaves the honest one, refused payload.
formats.x402_changes: for each x402 form, the authorization with one thing changed (each domain member, the primary type, each type's fields renamed, retyped, reordered, added and dropped, each message value, each time field one second later, the Permit2 address and proxy, the other form's schema) and its stream as the core would send it: consistent with the changed typed data, so only main's rebuild, before the first APDU, refuses it.
formats.byte_families: families too large to list, as rules over `honest`: the APDUs they change, how, and how many APDUs they make.

rules.parent: the APDU names a parent that is not live, not one of the rows' operations, or not for a Ledger account
rules.order: an APDU of the row out of its place: swapped, skipped, or the hash-only APDU without its 6D00 or before main's hash_only answer
rules.header: CLA INS P1 P2 that the row doesn't have at that point (E0 02 01 00 outside ledger.add among them), or an Lc that isn't the data's length
rules.count: an APDU the row sends once (the address check, B0 01, E0 0C), sent again
rules.path: another path where the row has P
rules.payload: the right header with other data: main's own stream, built from what it holds, has other bytes there
rules.ended: any APDU after the operation's last
